subject: Biotechnology
title: Gene Drives and Ecosystems
description: A fast breakdown of Gene Drives and Ecosystems for builders.

hook.text: Release one mosquito and change an entire species — gene drives spread engineered traits through wild populations.

buildup.text: CRISPR-based gene drives copy themselves to both chromosomes — guaranteeing inheritance in nearly 100% of offspring.

discovery.text: Target Malaria aims to suppress Anopheles mosquitoes — potentially saving 600,000 lives per year from malaria.

twist.text: Suppressing an entire species could cascade through food webs — bats, birds, and fish that eat mosquitoes lose a food source.

climax.text: Daisy-chain gene drives limit spread to a few generations — a self-limiting safeguard against permanent ecosystem change.

punchline.text: Edit a species or protect an ecosystem — gene drives force the biggest ecological gamble.

quiz.question: How do daisy-chain gene drives address ecological concerns?
options: They make the gene drive spread faster so the effect is over quickly
They limit the drive to a few generations before it disappears, preventing permanent species-wide changes
They only work on one specific mosquito species
